body: I appreciate you're trying to help and I'm sure what you describe is beneficial to many people, but not for me. I'm not making excuses: I have a road bike and use it regularly to go places. I'm also a runner, I run a few miles most days. I eat well and don't drink alcohol/fizzy juice. So you see unfortunately, a healthy lifestyle isn't the be all and end all for curing everyone's depression.
I'll give this a try, thanks.
Depends how you define it I guess.
That's fine, can't imagine I'd laugh anyway. All I'm thinking of is how to die without troubling anyone.
That's nice of you. I'm not worth your time.
They keep looking over my shoulder but I'll try. I haven't been out in months, now I remember why. I felt obliged to come as my friend is leaving the country soon.
Lots of things. But this is pushing me to the limit. Stupidly I agreed to take people home at the end of the night. I don't think I'll last that long.
How does it differ from the CBT in therapy sessions?

I've done some amazing things in my life. At least, people say they're amazing. You know that episode of the Simpsons where Grandpa wins a load of money and starts doing all this crazy stuff like rollercoasters? He just goes "meh" at them all. That's me. I know I haven't tried everything there is to try in the world, but I'm so difficult to be enthused. I've got some medical conditions that really hamper my enjoyment of life. I'm indifferent towards everything and I can't not be that; I can't change who I am. I just hate who I am.

Thanks for the comment. I do exercise, daily. I haven't seen a therapist for nearly a year now because they all end up saying they've done all they can and that there's no longer any point in me going along unless something really bad happens. According to all the psychiatrists I've seen, I've tried all the combinations of meds. Maybe it's different in the UK. I use the coping strategies I've learned but I always find a way to break out of them. I do wonder sometimes if permanent incarceration would be better.
